newsitem.title: UK: Don't retaliate, UK minister asks Protestants.
newsitem.headline: Don't retaliate, UK minister asks Protestants.

text.p: Northern Ireland Minister Michael Ancram on Tuesday pleaded with Protestant guerrillas not to retaliate after a suspected Irish Republican bomb attack on British army headquarters in the province injured 31 people.

"I call on particularly the Loyalist (pro-British) paramilitaries not to fall into the trap of those who planted those devices with murderous intent and maintain their ceasefire," he told BBC Radio after Monday's blasts.

Ancram said: "It is a dire challenge to the peace process. There is no doubt that whoever planted these devices was intent on blowing the process which is taking place at the moment out of the water."
He conceded that the security breach of the army's nerve centre in Northern Ireland was "a matter of grave concern".

It was the first time in more than two years that a British security target had been hit in the province and raised fears among politicians and the province's 1.5 million people of a return to a 27-year conflict which killed 3,200.
The bombing caused immediate speculation there would be resumed activity by pro-British guerrillas who killed 900 Catholics in a tit-for-tat war before calling a truce two years ago.

Ancram, also interviewed by BBC television, said: "The Loyalist paramilitaries have maintained their ceasefire. I believe that this is a trap to try and entice them to drop their ceasefire and I call on them very strongly not to fall into that trap."
